Once you have opened a machine and seen how it is built, you look for products that are {{7}} rather than sealed shut, and you become less willing to {{8}} a device that still has years of use. Manufacturers notice this: some now publish manuals and sell parts directly to customers, a policy that would have seemed odd a generation ago.

None of this will {{9}} the problem of electronic waste alone. But every object kept in use is one that does not reach the bin, and the habit of mending is {{10}} in a world of limited resources.

blanks.explain: discard that habit 意为“抛弃那个习惯”，与后文 fix things instead 形成对比；nod、edit 语义不合。
more affordable than buying another 指“比再买一个更负担得起”，与整段关于金钱的讨论一致。
learn a skill that their grandparents took for granted 指学习祖辈视为理所当然的“技能”；lecture 不合。
Experienced volunteers sit at long tables 指有经验的“志愿者”坐在长桌旁；lecture 无法指人。
find guidance from someone 表示从他人那里得到“指导”；hesitate 是动词，不能作宾语。
leave more confident 指离开时更“自信”，与 arrive convinced that they are useless 形成对照。
products that are durable rather than sealed shut 指“耐用”、可维修而非封死不可拆的产品。
less willing to replace a device that still has years of use 指不愿“更换”仍能用的设备，与上文的选购倾向呼应；edit、nod 不合。
solve the problem of electronic waste 是固定搭配，表示“解决电子垃圾问题”；nod、edit 不合。
the habit of mending is essential 指修补的习惯“必不可少”，与 limited resources 的语境呼应。

items.title: Museums Beyond the Glass Case
items.passage:
For generations the museum visit followed a simple rule: look, but do not touch. Objects sat behind glass, labels supplied dates, and visitors moved through rooms in silence. That model still suits many collections, yet it excludes anyone who cannot see well and leaves most people with only a faint impression of the past.

Designers have begun to {{1}} the experience. Some galleries now provide {{2}} copies of sculptures that visitors may handle, with labels in larger print and plain language. Others use sound: a recording of a workshop or the murmur of a market can {{3}} a scene more vividly than text.

The change is not only about disability. Curators have found that a multi-sensory room holds school groups far longer than a case of objects, and that families stay until closing. When a visitor can lift a replica sword or smell the resin used in a boat, the past becomes something like a memory.

Critics warn that replicas may {{4}} real objects in the minds of visitors, and that a museum should not {{5}} scholarship for novelty. Curators answer that the two goals are not in {{6}}. A careful reconstruction, they argue, draws attention to the original rather than {{7}} its importance. Many institutions now label replicas clearly and invite visitors to compare the copy with the genuine item.

The biggest {{8}} is training. Front-of-house staff need time to {{9}} new formats, and small museums often lack the money to build them. Still, the principle is hard to {{10}}: a collection that few people can fully experience serves the public less well than one that welcomes everybody.

blanks.explain: begun to rethink the experience 指开始“重新思考”参观体验，后文列举的新做法与之一致；wander、publish 不合。
tactile copies 指可供触摸的“触觉”复制品，与 may handle 直接呼应；sudden、ceiling 不合。
evoke a scene 表示声音能“唤起”场景，比文字更生动；publish、fold 不能与 scene 构成此义。
displace real objects 指复制品可能“取代”真品在观众心中的位置，与 critics warn 的语气一致。
sacrifice scholarship for novelty 指为了新奇而“牺牲”学术性，搭配成立；wander、fold 不合。
not in conflict 表示两个目标并不“冲突”，与 Curators answer 的辩护逻辑一致；ceiling 不合。
rather than diminish its importance 指复制品应突出而不是“削弱”原件的重要性，与 draws attention to 形成对比；displace 不能与 its importance 搭配。
The biggest obstacle is training 指最大的“障碍”是培训，后文提到人手与经费，语义连贯。
adopt new formats 指员工需要时间“采用”新形式，搭配自然；fold、wander 不合。
the principle is hard to dispute 意为这一原则“难以反驳”，冒号后的解释即其理由。

items.title: Birdsong in the City
items.passage:
Early in the morning, before the streets fill, a city can sound almost like a forest. Blackbirds, sparrows, and gulls sing from rooftops and plane trees, and for a few minutes the {{1}} of traffic is drowned out. City dwellers who notice this are often surprised, because the common view is that wildlife belongs to the countryside.

The truth is more interesting. Cities support fewer species than forests, but the birds that do live there are often remarkably {{2}}. Some have learned to sing at a higher pitch so that their songs can be heard above low engine {{3}}. Others have shifted the hours of their dawn chorus, starting earlier when the background is quieter. Such adjustments happen over decades rather than overnight, yet they show how quickly animals can {{4}} to an artificial environment.

For humans the benefits run the other way. Many office workers and hospital patients say that a view of greenery, or even a recording of birdsong, can {{5}} recovery and calm the nerves. This may explain why urban planners now {{6}} parks and green roofs not as decoration but as public health measures.

None of this happens by accident. A city that {{7}} nature needs space for insects, water for drinking, and trees old enough to shelter nests. It also needs residents who will {{8}} the racket their own machinery makes. Several councils have placed a {{9}} on building work during the breeding season, and some have dimmed street lights to help birds rest.

Such measures are cheap compared with the cost of a city that has {{10}} its birds, where the only sound is the traffic that drove them away.

blanks.explain: the {{1}} of traffic 需要名词，指车流的“轰鸣声”，与 drowned out 搭配；lecture 不合语义。
后文说鸟改变音高、提前鸣唱，说明它们“适应力强”，adaptable 正确；fragile 与这些证据相反。
low engine noise 指发动机的低频“噪音”，与上文 sound、pitch 的话题一致；lecture 不能形容发动机。
can 后接动词原形，adjust to 表示“适应”，与 such adjustments 呼应；wander、fold 不接 to。
speed 作动词意为“加速”，speed recovery 是固定搭配；punish、fold 与 recovery 不能搭配。
treat...as 表示“把……视为”，与 not as decoration but as public health measures 的结构吻合。
主语 A city 为单数，故用第三人称单数 welcomes，意为“接纳自然”；punish 与 needs space... 的语境相反。
reduce the racket 表示“减少喧闹声”，与后文限制施工、调暗路灯的措施并列。
place a ban on building work 指在繁殖季“禁止”施工，固定搭配且与保护鸟类的目的相符；lecture 与语境无关。
has lost its birds 用现在完成时表示“已经失去”鸟类，与后文“只剩车流声”构成对照。

items.title: Gardens Above the Street
items.passage:
Look down on a modern city from a high window and you will see a grey landscape of roofs. Look again in a few years and some of those roofs may have turned green. Rooftop gardens, once a novelty on expensive apartment blocks, are spreading to schools, offices, and public housing, and they are changing the way cities {{1}} heat, water, and food.

The environmental case is easy to {{2}}. A layer of soil and plants absorbs sunlight that would otherwise be {{3}} by concrete, so the building below stays cooler in summer. The plants also slow rainwater, which {{4}} the pressure on drains during storms. In dense neighbourhoods where ground space is scarce, a roof may be the only {{5}} place to grow vegetables.

The social case is less obvious but just as {{6}}. A shared garden gives neighbours a reason to talk, and a school roof can become an outdoor classroom where children learn where food comes from. Tenants who have never met may find themselves {{7}} tomatoes together on a Saturday morning.

Rooftop gardens are not {{8}}, however. The structure must carry the weight of wet soil, the waterproofing must be perfect, and someone must water the plants in dry spells. Costs can {{9}} quickly, and a poorly planned garden may be abandoned within a season.

Cities that have made the gardens work usually started small. A single pilot roof allowed engineers to test the load, gardeners to learn which plants {{10}} the wind, and residents to see the benefit for themselves. Success then spread by example rather than by rule.

blanks.explain: the way cities manage heat, water, and food 指城市“管理”热、水和食物的方式；publish、punish 语义不合。
make the case 意为“提出理由、论证”，与 the environmental case 搭配；wander、publish 不合。
would otherwise be absorbed by concrete 指阳光本会被混凝土“吸收”，被动语态需过去分词。
which 指代前面的做法，从句谓语用第三人称单数 reduces，表示“减轻”排水压力。
the only available place 指“唯一可用的地方”，与 ground space is scarce 呼应；fragile、sudden 不合。
just as strong 与 less obvious 形成转折，指社会层面的理由“同样有力”；fragile 语义相反。
find themselves planting tomatoes 表示“发现自己正在种西红柿”，需现在分词；publish 不合。
not simple 后列举承重、防水、浇水等难题，说明屋顶花园并不“简单”；sudden 不合。
costs can rise 表示“成本会上升”，与后文花园被弃用形成因果；publish、wander 不合。
plants resist the wind 指植物“抵御”风力，作定语从句谓语；punish、publish 不合。

items.title: Letters in the Drawer
items.passage:
A handwritten letter arrives slowly. It may take days to reach its reader, and its paper carries the marks of a particular day: a smudge, a crossed-out word, a change of pen. In an age of {{1}} messages, that slowness looks like a fault. Yet people who write letters by hand describe the practice as a form of {{2}} that no screen can imitate.

The difference begins with time. Typing a message encourages a quick reply, while writing by hand forces the writer to {{3}} each sentence before it is committed to paper. The hand moves more slowly than the mind, and that gap gives the writer room to {{4}} what is worth saying. Many letter writers say their real thoughts appear only after the second page.

A letter also lasts. Emails pile up in an inbox and are rarely read twice, whereas a letter can be kept in a drawer for years. Grandchildren may one day {{5}} a bundle of envelopes and learn what their grandparents were like as young people. In this sense, a letter is less a message than a small {{6}} of a life.

Handwriting itself carries meaning. A hasty scrawl suggests impatience; a careful loop suggests care. None of this can be conveyed by a standard font, however {{7}} the design. The reader hears a voice even though nothing is spoken.

None of this means that digital messages are {{8}}. They are simply different tools, suited to different tasks. The {{9}} is to keep both: a quick note to confirm a meeting, and, now and then, a letter that shows someone you were willing to spend an {{10}} on them.

blanks.explain: an age of instant messages 指“即时消息”的时代，与 slowness 形成对比；sudden、elegant 不合。
a form of patience 指写信是一种“耐心”的体现，呼应慢、需等待的特点；lecture、furniture 不合。
forces the writer to weigh each sentence 指被迫“权衡”每个句子，与手写速度慢的语境一致。
room to discover what is worth saying 指有空间“发现自己”真正想说的话；descend、punish 不合。
grandchildren may inherit a bundle of envelopes 指孙辈可能“继承”一捆信件，符合代际传递的语境。
a small record of a life 指信是人生的“记录”，与上句 kept in a drawer for years 呼应。
however elegant the design 指无论字体设计多么“优雅”，都无法传达手写的意味；sudden 不合。
否定句意为数字消息并非“毫无价值”，后文 They are simply different tools 正是解释。
The answer is to keep both 指应对办法是两者兼用；lecture、furniture 不能表达“办法”。
spend an afternoon on them 指愿意为某人花“一个下午”写信；冠词 an 也排除 lecture 等词。

items.title: The Usefulness of Boredom
items.passage:
Reach for a phone whenever a queue forms or a train stops in a tunnel, and you will rarely be bored. That reflex has become so {{1}} that many people cannot remember the last time they sat with nothing to do. The result may be a quiet loss of something valuable.

Boredom has a bad name, and for good reason: nobody enjoys the restless feeling of a dull afternoon. Yet boredom is also a signal. It tells us that the current activity is not {{2}} us, and it pushes us to look for something better. In that sense it works like pain, which we dislike but which keeps us from harm.

The trouble is that we now treat every gap in the day as a problem to be {{3}}. A moment of inactivity is filled with a video, a game, or a stream of messages. Convenient as this is, it may {{4}} the mind's habit of wandering. When the brain is not occupied by a task, it {{5}} to connect ideas that seemed unrelated, and these connections are the raw material of {{6}}.

Psychologists who study attention suggest a simple experiment. Leave the phone in another room for an hour and see what happens. The first ten minutes may feel {{7}}. Then the mind begins to drift, and the drift is not a failure; it is the mind exercising. People who {{8}} this practice often report that they notice details around them and arrive at solutions they had been {{9}} for days.

None of this argues for a duller life. It argues for a life with more {{10}} between the interesting parts.

blanks.explain: so automatic 指掏手机已变成“下意识的”反应，与 cannot remember the last time 呼应；sudden 不合。
not rewarding us 指当前活动“不能带来回报”，所以无聊会推动我们寻找更好的事；annual 不合。
a problem to be solved 是常见搭配，指每个空档都被当作“要解决的问题”；folded、punished 不合。
it may weaken the mind's habit 指用视频填满空档可能“削弱”大脑走神的习惯；punish 不合。
it tends to connect ideas 表示大脑“倾向于”把不相干的想法联系起来，主语为 it。
the raw material of creativity 指这些联系是“创造力”的原料；ceiling 不合。
feel unbearable 指最初的十分钟可能“难以忍受”，与后文 Then the mind begins to drift 形成转折。
people who maintain this practice 指“坚持”这种做法的人；punish、fold 语义不合。
solutions they had been seeking for days 指苦寻数日的答案，过去完成进行时需现在分词。
more space between the interesting parts 指在有趣之事之间留出“空白”，与全文倡导的留白呼应。

items.title: The Recycling Club
items.passage:
At the start of the school year, a group of students noticed something simple. Every lunchtime, the bins outside the dining hall were filled with paper cups, plastic bottles, and half-eaten sandwiches. The students decided to start a recycling club, and within a term it had changed the habits of the whole school.

The first step was to {{1}} what was actually being thrown away. For a week, members wore gloves and sorted the rubbish from one bin into different boxes. The results were {{2}}: more than half of it could have been reused or recycled. The club put the boxes in the hall so that everyone could see them, and the {{3}} made a stronger impression than any poster.

Next came the practical part. The club asked the school to put separate bins in every corridor and to {{4}} the staff about what belonged where. They also wrote a short guide and {{5}} it to each classroom. Some teachers were {{6}} at first, because the new system took time, but most agreed once they saw how much waste had {{7}}.

The club did not stop at lunchtime. Members visited younger classes to talk about the {{8}} of throwing everything into one bin, and they organised a day when students brought old books and clothes to school for others to take home. The event was so {{9}} that the school has decided to hold it twice a year.

What began as a small idea has become part of the timetable. The students say the biggest {{10}} is not money but patience: habits change slowly, and a club needs members who will keep going when the first excitement fades.

blanks.explain: the first step was to survey what was thrown away 指先“调查”被丢弃的东西，与 a week of sorting 呼应。
结果“令人吃惊”：一半以上本可回收，因此填 surprising；narrow 无法表达这种出乎意料。
the sight made a stronger impression 指“看到的景象”比海报更有冲击力，与 everyone could see them 呼应。
remind the staff about... 表示“提醒”员工；borrow、fold 不能接 about。
wrote a short guide and delivered it to each classroom 指把指南“送”到每个教室；borrowed 与语境不符。
some teachers were doubtful at first 指老师起初“怀疑”，与后文 most agreed once... 形成转折。
how much waste had dropped 表示垃圾量“下降”了，与回收系统生效的语境一致。
the harm of throwing everything into one bin 指混投垃圾的“害处”，是向低年级宣传的重点。
the event was so popular that... 指活动“受欢迎”，所以学校决定一年办两次。
the biggest challenge is not money but patience 指最大的“挑战”是耐心，冒号后解释了原因。

items.title: A Town Learns to Cycle
items.passage:
Ten years ago, most people in this town drove to work, even when the journey was only a few minutes long. Today the picture looks different. A new cycle path runs beside the river, the office car park is half empty, and warm mornings bring bicycles into town. The change did not happen by itself.

The council began by making cycling safer. It {{1}} the busiest street so that cars had less space and bikes had a lane. It also added a bridge over the ring road, which {{2}} the most dangerous part of the journey. At first, shop owners were {{3}} that fewer parking spaces would mean fewer customers, but the opposite proved true: cyclists stopped more often than drivers.

Employers helped as well. Several offices installed showers and secure racks, and a few now {{4}} staff a small sum for every day they cycle. One manager explained that cyclists arrive more {{5}} and take fewer sick days, so the money is well spent.

Not everyone is {{6}} that cycling is safe, of course. Older residents and parents of young children still find the traffic frightening, and the town has not yet {{7}} enough pavements. The council plans to spend the next year {{8}} the gaps in the network, starting near schools.

What has changed most is how people think about cyclists. Riders were once seen as a small group in special clothing; now they are ordinary people carrying shopping or heading to work. That change in {{9}} may be as important as the new path. A town that once laughed at cycling now {{10}} it as a normal way to travel.

blanks.explain: narrowed the busiest street 指把最繁忙的街道“改窄”，以便给自行车留出车道。
which removed the most dangerous part 指新桥“消除了”最危险的路段；folded、published 不合。
shop owners were worried that... 指店主“担心”停车位减少会流失顾客；wooden 不能修饰人的情绪。
a few now pay staff a small sum 表示公司“支付”员工一小笔钱，与后文 the money is well spent 呼应。
cyclists arrive more alert 指骑车上班的人到岗时更“清醒”，所以请病假更少。
not everyone is convinced that cycling is safe 指并非所有人都“相信”骑车安全，后文老居民和家长的担心正是例证。
has not yet built enough pavements 指小镇还没“修建”足够的人行道，现在完成时用过去分词。
spend the next year closing the gaps 指花一年时间“填补”路网空白，spend time doing 结构。
that change in attitude 指人们对骑车者“态度”的转变，与前文 once seen as... now... 对应。
treats it as a normal way to travel 指小镇如今把骑车“视为”正常出行方式；publishes、folds 不合。

items.title: A Notebook by the Bed
items.passage:
Many people buy a notebook in January, write in it for a week, and then leave it in a drawer. Keeping a diary sounds easy, but it asks for a habit that most of us never build. Those who do keep one often say the same thing: the value comes not from style but from {{1}}.

A diary does not need to be a work of art. You can {{2}} down a few lines about what you ate, who you met, or how you felt. The point is to {{3}} the day before it disappears. Memory is {{4}}, and small details that seem unimportant today may be the ones you most want to read in ten years.

There are practical {{5}}, too. Writing about a worry can make it smaller, because putting it into words {{6}} you to see its shape. Some doctors even suggest a diary for people who find it hard to sleep, since a page of notes can {{7}} the mind for rest.

The habit is easier to keep if you make it {{8}}. Keep the notebook beside your bed, choose a fixed time, and do not worry about grammar. If you miss a day, simply start again; nobody is marking your work. It also pays to write in the same {{9}} each time, so that opening the notebook becomes a signal that the day is over.

After a year, the reward is clear. You will have a record of ordinary life that no photograph can {{10}}, and you may understand yourself a little better than when you began.

blanks.explain: the value comes not from style but from practice 指写日记的价值来自“坚持练习”，而非文笔。
jot down a few lines 是固定搭配，意为“随手记下几行”；publish、punish 不能接 down。
capture the day before it disappears 指在一天消失前“捕捉”它，形象地表达记录的作用。
memory is selective 指记忆是“有选择的”，所以小细节日后可能格外珍贵；wooden 不合。
there are practical benefits 指写日记有实际的“好处”，需要复数名词，后文列举的正是这些好处。
putting it into words helps you to see its shape 指把烦恼写下来“有助于”看清它的形状。
settle the mind for rest 指让大脑“安定”下来准备休息，与睡眠话题一致。
make it simple 指把写日记这件事变得“简单”，后文的建议都是简化做法。
write in the same place each time 指每次在同一个“地方”写，与 opening the notebook becomes a signal 呼应。
a record that no photograph can match 指照片也无法“比得上”的记录；publish、punish 不合。

items.title: Saturday at the Shelter
items.passage:
Every Saturday morning, a small group of people gathers at the animal shelter on the edge of town. They are not staff. They are {{1}}, and they come to walk dogs, clean cages, and spend time with cats that have been waiting a long time for a home.

Most of them started with a simple wish to help, and discovered that the work {{2}} more than it takes. Dogs that are walked regularly become {{3}} and easier to adopt. Cats that are touched every day learn to trust people again. A helper who arrives feeling tired often leaves feeling {{4}}, because the animals do not care about the problems waiting at home.

The shelter's manager says the helpers are {{5}} to its survival. The budget covers food and medical care, but there is never enough money for extra staff. Without people who {{6}} their free time, many animals would spend whole days alone.

Volunteering is not always {{7}}. Some animals are frightened, some are sick, and a few cannot be adopted at all. New helpers are trained to {{8}} the rules: wash your hands, watch your fingers, and never open a cage without asking. It can be {{9}} at first, but most people find the routine satisfying.

The shelter also asks its helpers to {{10}} the message that an animal is a long-term responsibility. A puppy given as a gift may be abandoned by winter. If more people understood that, fewer dogs would be waiting on a Saturday morning.

blanks.explain: They are not staff. They are volunteers 指他们不是员工而是“志愿者”，需要复数名词。
the work gives more than it takes 指这份工作“给予”的比索取的多，主语 the work 决定用第三人称单数。
dogs become calmer 指被经常遛的狗变得更“平静”，也更容易被领养；wooden、annual 不合。
leaves feeling cheerful 指离开时感到“愉快”，与 arrives feeling tired 形成对比。
volunteers are essential to its survival 指志愿者对收容所的存续“必不可少”，后文说明人手不足。
people who donate their free time 指“捐出”业余时间的人，与志愿工作的性质吻合。
not always pleasant 指志愿工作并不总是“愉快的”，后面列举了害怕、生病的动物。
trained to follow the rules 指接受培训以“遵守”规则，冒号后正是具体规定。
it can be confusing at first 指一开始可能“令人困惑”，与后文 most people find the routine satisfying 转折。
spread the message 指“传播”这一信息，即养宠物是长期责任；postpone、punish 不合。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 01
items.passage:
短文：
Many students now type their lecture notes on a laptop, yet a growing number of teachers encourage them to write by hand. One reason is speed: typing allows a student to record almost every word, but this can actually {{1}} understanding. When people write slowly, they must decide what matters and express it in their own words, which makes the material easier to {{2}} later. A study at an American university found that students who took notes by hand performed better on questions that required them to explain ideas, although the two groups scored {{3}} on simple factual questions. Handwriting also seems to keep the mind from {{4}} during long lectures, because the writer cannot simply copy words without thinking. Of course, laptops remain {{5}} for courses with large amounts of data, and no teacher should {{6}} students who genuinely need them. The {{7}} message is that the method matters less than the thinking behind it. Teachers can help by {{8}} fewer but better questions and by giving students time after class to {{9}} their notes with a partner. In the end, good notes are not a {{10}} of the lecture but a record of the student's own ideas.

blanks.explain: 选 I. hinder。hinder 意为“阻碍、妨碍”，hinder understanding 指反而妨碍理解；benefit 虽也可接宾语，但与句中 but 的转折逻辑相反。
选 L. recall。recall 意为“回想起、忆起”，与后面的 later 呼应，说明用自己的话记笔记能帮助日后回忆内容。
选 E. equally。空格修饰动词 scored，需要程度副词；equally 表示两组在简单事实题上“得分相同”，与 although 引导的让步关系一致。
选 O. wandering。keep sb from doing sth 为固定结构，wandering 指“走神、思绪游移”，说明手写让人无法不假思索地抄写，从而保持专注。
选 N. useful。remain 后接形容词作表语，useful 表示笔记本电脑在数据量大的课程中仍然“有用”，与前面的转折语气相符。
选 G. forbid。forbid sb to do sth 意为“禁止某人做某事”，此处指不应禁止确实需要笔记本电脑的学生使用它。
选 H. general。the general message 意为“总的信息、总体结论”，空格需形容词修饰 message，概括前文的对比。
选 A. asking。by 后接动名词，ask questions 意为“提问”，fewer but better questions 说明问题应少而精。
选 C. compare。compare A with B 意为“把 A 与 B 作比较”，与 with a partner 搭配，指课后和同伴对照、补充笔记。
选 D. copy。a copy of the lecture 意为“讲义的复制品”，与后面的 a record of the student's own ideas 形成对比。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 02
items.passage:
短文：
Watching films is one of the most enjoyable ways to learn a foreign language, but it works best when it is done with some {{1}}. Many learners simply switch on the subtitles in their own language and follow the story, which is entertaining but does little for their vocabulary. A better method is to watch a short scene twice: first with English subtitles and then without. On the second viewing, the brain is forced to {{2}} the sound of words with their meaning. It also helps to {{3}} difficult expressions in a notebook and to look them up afterwards. Research on vocabulary learning suggests that a word must be met many times before it is remembered, so choosing one film and watching it again after a week may be more {{4}} than watching five new films in a row. Teachers warn, however, that films should not {{5}} other kinds of practice. Speaking, reading and writing still need time. Used {{6}}, though, films can bring the language to life and remind learners why they are studying it. The {{7}} of the story also gives the brain something to hold on to, which makes new words easier to {{8}}. In short, films are not a {{9}} for hard work, but a {{10}} that makes the work more pleasant.

blanks.explain: 选 H. planning。with some planning 意为“有所计划”，与后文“不要只是打开母语字幕看故事”形成对比，空格需名词。
选 B. connect。connect A with B 意为“把 A 与 B 联系起来”，指把词的读音与意义对应起来，是语言学习的常用搭配。
选 J. record。record ... in a notebook 意为“把……记在笔记本里”，与 look them up afterwards 前后衔接；retain 强调记住，不接 in a notebook。
选 C. effective。more effective than 为比较级结构，effective 意为“有效的”，说明重复看同一部电影的学习效果可能更好。
选 K. replace。replace 意为“取代”，句中说明电影不应取代说、读、写等其他形式的练习，与后文 Speaking, reading and writing still need time 呼应。
选 O. wisely。used wisely 为过去分词短语作状语，意为“如果使用得当”，需要副词修饰 used。
选 I. plot。the plot of the story 意为“故事情节”，情节为大脑提供线索，使新词更容易记住。
选 L. retain。retain 意为“记住、保持”，easier to retain 表示新词更容易记住；record 强调记录动作，与“记住”语义不同。
选 M. substitute。a substitute for sth 意为“某物的替代品”，此处说明电影不能代替刻苦学习。
选 N. tool。a tool that makes the work more pleasant 意为“一种让学习更愉快的工具”，与前半句 not a substitute 形成对比。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 03
items.passage:
短文：
Every year the world produces far more clothes than people can wear. Prices are low, designs change quickly, and a T-shirt may be worn a few times before it is {{1}} away. The results are easy to see: mountains of clothing in landfills and rivers polluted by the dyes used in factories. Some companies have begun to {{2}} the problem by collecting old clothes in their shops, but only a small share of what is collected is turned into new fabric. Most is sold to other countries or burned. Consumers have more {{3}} than they realise. Washing clothes at a lower temperature and drying them in the air can {{4}} their life by years, and simple repairs can save a favourite jacket from the bin. Buying {{5}}, well-made clothes costs more at first but saves money later. Campaigners also encourage people to organise swap events, where friends bring clothes they no longer wear and take home something {{6}}. None of these actions is {{7}} on its own, but together they {{8}} the pressure on the planet. The most {{9}} change, campaigners argue, is to buy less and choose {{10}}.

blanks.explain: 选 M. thrown。be thrown away 意为“被扔掉”，与上衣只穿几次就被丢弃的语境一致，空格需过去分词构成被动。
选 L. tackle。tackle the problem 意为“应对、处理问题”，与 by collecting old clothes 的方式说明相搭配。
选 H. power。have more power than they realise 意为“拥有比自己意识到的更大的影响力”，指消费者可以通过选择影响环境。
选 F. extend。extend 意为“延长”，extend the life of clothes by years 即“把衣服的寿命延长数年”。
选 B. durable。durable 意为“耐穿的、结实的”，与 well-made 并列修饰 clothes；虽然初期花费更高，但此后更省钱。
选 A. different。something different 意为“不一样的东西”，说明交换活动让旧衣换成别的衣物，减少购买。
选 D. enough。none of these actions is enough on its own 意为“单靠其中任何一项都不够”，与 but 后的 together 形成对比。
选 J. reduce。reduce the pressure on the planet 意为“减轻对地球的压力”，是常见的动宾搭配。
选 C. effective。the most effective change 意为“最有效的改变”，形容词最高级修饰 change，表示倡导者认为最管用的做法。
选 N. wisely。choose wisely 意为“明智地选择”，需要副词修饰动词 choose，与 buy less 并列说明消费态度。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 04
items.passage:
短文：
Every city has buildings that tell its story, yet many of them disappear before residents have time to think. In the past, planners often {{1}} that old structures were simply in the way of progress. Today a different view is spreading, and heritage protection has become an {{2}} part of urban planning.

Repair is rarely cheap. A stone arch or a wooden roof may need months of work by specialists whose skills are in short {{3}}. Supporters say repair costs far less than loss. Once a building is gone, the stories attached to it are {{4}} as well.

Some cities have found {{5}} solutions. In one old district, a former textile factory became a library. Tourists come, but the {{6}} visitors are local people who use the reading rooms every day. The project also provided {{7}} work for craftsmen who might otherwise have left the area.

Critics still {{8}} that such projects mainly attract wealthy newcomers and push poorer residents out. That risk is real, and it must be {{9}} seriously. But the answer is not to demolish everything; it is to plan carefully and accept that a city without memory is {{10}} to lose its identity.

blanks.explain: 选 D. claimed（对应第 26 空）。空格需填过去式动词，claim that... 表示‘声称’，与 In the past 的时态一致。
选 F. essential（对应第 27 空）。an essential part of 意为‘……不可或缺的一部分’，与‘观念正在传播’的语境一致。
选 N. supply（对应第 28 空）。in short supply 是固定搭配，意为‘供不应求、十分稀缺’，说明掌握这类技艺的专家很少。
选 G. forgotten（对应第 29 空）。are forgotten 为被动语态，与前半句 Once a building is gone 对应，表示故事也随之被遗忘。
选 E. creative（对应第 30 空）。下文把旧纺织厂改成图书馆即为‘有创意的’做法，creative 修饰 solutions 最贴切。
选 L. regular（对应第 31 空）。regular visitors 指‘常客’，与后文‘每天都来阅览室’呼应，并与游客形成对比。
选 M. steady（对应第 32 空）。steady work 意为‘稳定的工作’，正因工作稳定，工匠才不必离开此地。
选 B. argue（对应第 33 空）。argue that 表示‘认为、主张’，此处引出批评者的观点。
选 J. handled（对应第 34 空）。be handled seriously 意为‘被认真对待、处理’，情态动词 must 后接过去分词构成被动。
选 K. likely（对应第 35 空）。be likely to do 意为‘很可能……’，作者借此强调保护城市记忆的重要性。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 05
items.passage:
短文：
Volunteering is usually described as a gift of time, but its benefits do not flow in one direction only. Students who spend a few hours a week at a community centre often say they gain as much as they {{1}}. The first weeks, though, can feel {{2}}: a new place, unfamiliar faces and tasks that look simple but are not.

What makes the difference is {{3}} — turning up every week rather than once, when nothing else is planned. Organisers say the most {{4}} volunteers are not always the most talented ones, but those who keep their promises.

Volunteering also teaches skills that are hard to {{5}} in a classroom, such as listening patiently and explaining an idea in simple words. Employers have begun to {{6}} such experience, and some universities now {{7}} volunteer work in the record students take to interviews.

There are limits, of course. Volunteering should not {{8}} the place of paid work, nor should it damage a student's studies. What {{9}} is a modest but steady commitment, and the habit, once {{10}}, often lasts for life.

blanks.explain: 选 D. give（对应第 26 空）。gain as much as they give 意为‘收获与付出一样多’，与前半句 benefits do not flow in one direction only 呼应。
选 A. awkward（对应第 27 空）。冒号后列举‘陌生的地方、陌生的面孔’，说明最初几周会感到别扭、不自在。
选 B. consistency（对应第 28 空）。破折号后的解释‘每周都来，而不是没别的事才来一次’正是 consistency（坚持一致）的含义。
选 J. reliable（对应第 29 空）。but those who keep their promises 说明组织者看重的是‘可靠’，与 talented 形成对比。
选 F. learn（对应第 30 空）。‘在课堂上难以学到的技能’与后文列举的倾听、解释能力相配，learn 与 skills 构成动宾搭配。
选 I. recognise（对应第 31 空）。recognise 在此意为‘认可、重视’，表示雇主开始看重这类经历。
选 E. include（对应第 32 空）。include A in B 意为‘把 A 列入 B’，即把志愿工作写入求职材料。
选 L. take（对应第 33 空）。take the place of 意为‘取代’，本句表示志愿服务不应取代有报酬的工作。
选 G. matters（对应第 34 空）。What matters is... 意为‘重要的是……’，总结全文对志愿服务的态度。
选 C. formed（对应第 35 空）。once formed 为‘连词 + 过去分词’结构，表示习惯一旦养成便会持续一生。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 06
items.passage:
短文：
Researchers who study body language like to remind us that words carry only part of any message. The rest comes from the face, the hands and the distance we keep from other people. A gesture that is friendly in one country can cause {{1}} in another; a distance that feels natural may make another person {{2}}.

This does not mean that body language is a list of rules to be learned {{3}}. Most people manage it unconsciously. If a visitor keeps {{4}} his hands and shifting his feet, we may decide, without any {{5}}, that he is nervous or dishonest, when he is simply cold or tired.

The {{6}} advice is therefore to slow down. Watch how people sit and how long they look at each other. Ask a colleague whether a habit that seems natural to you is {{7}} in the new setting. Above all, do not {{8}} politeness with agreement: a person may be extremely polite and still firmly refuse your idea.

None of this is {{9}}. Reading the wrong signal is a mistake everyone makes, and the ability to laugh at one's own {{10}} is itself a form of cultural skill.

blanks.explain: 选 H. offence（对应第 26 空）。cause offence 意为‘冒犯他人’，与前半句 friendly 形成对比，故用名词 offence。
选 N. uncomfortable（对应第 27 空）。make sb + 形容词表示‘使某人……’，此处指你觉得自然的距离会让对方不舒服。
选 I. overnight（对应第 28 空）。learned overnight 意为‘一夜之间学会’，与后文‘人们是无意识地掌握它的’形成对照。
选 K. rubbing（对应第 29 空）。keep doing sth 后接动名词，rub one's hands（搓手）与 shifting his feet 并列，均为紧张的外在表现。
选 E. evidence（对应第 30 空）。without any evidence 意为‘没有任何证据’，说明这种判断只是主观印象。
选 L. simplest（对应第 31 空）。下文给出的都是‘放慢速度’一类朴素做法，故用形容词最高级 simplest 修饰 advice。
选 A. acceptable（对应第 32 空）。be acceptable in a setting 意为‘在某种场合可以被接受’，符合‘向同事确认习惯是否得体’之意。
选 C. confuse（对应第 33 空）。confuse A with B 意为‘把 A 与 B 混为一谈’，冒号后的解释说明礼貌并不等于同意。
选 D. easy（对应第 34 空）。后文说读错信号是人人都会犯的错，说明这并不容易，用 easy 与前面‘放慢速度’的建议相呼应。
选 F. mistakes（对应第 35 空）。laugh at one's own mistakes 意为‘笑对自己的错误’，复数与 one's own 搭配，也与前文 a mistake everyone makes 对应。

items.title: Reading Section A 选词填空
items.paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 07
items.passage:
Many adults believe that learning to play a musical instrument is a task for children, yet a growing body of research {{1}} that the adult brain is far more adaptable than was once thought. Teachers of adult beginners report that their students are often more {{2}} than teenagers, because they choose to be there.

The main {{3}} for adults is time. Work and family duties leave little space for daily practice, and progress can seem painfully slow. Teachers therefore {{4}} short, frequent sessions rather than one long one at the weekend. Fifteen minutes a day is enough to {{5}} a new habit.

Adults also tend to be hard on themselves. A wrong note that a child barely notices may make an adult want to give up entirely. Experienced teachers {{6}} this anxiety by choosing simple pieces at first and by celebrating small improvements.

The benefits go beyond music. Studies {{7}} that playing an instrument engages memory, attention and coordination at the same time. Some researchers {{8}} that this mental exercise may help keep the brain healthy in later life, although the evidence is not yet {{9}}.

What is clear is that adults who begin lessons rarely {{10}} the decision, even if they never perform in public.

blanks.explain: 选 O. suggests。research 为不可数名词作主语，谓语用第三人称单数，且后接 that 从句表示研究结果显示；indicate 形式不符，故排除。
选 H. motivated。be more motivated than 表示比青少年更有动力，与后半句 because they choose to be there 相呼应；permanent 不能修饰人的学习状态。
选 I. obstacle。the main obstacle 意为主要障碍，后文说工作与家庭占去练习时间，正是成年人学琴的主要困难；roughly 是副词，不能作主语。
选 K. recommend。recommend A rather than B 意为建议选 A 而不选 B，符合教师给成年初学者的练习建议；delay 与句意相反。
选 E. establish。establish a habit 是固定搭配，意为养成新习惯；achieve 通常接 goal 或 success，不与 habit 搭配。

items.passage:

Second, compare the same kind of product rather than two different foods, because {{4}} values are easier to judge.

Nutritionists advise shoppers to {{5}} products with a long list of unfamiliar ingredients. Usually a short list means the food has been processed less. They also {{6}} that sugar appears under many names, so a product may contain three kinds of sweetener and still look {{7}} at first glance.

Food companies argue that labels give consumers {{8}} to make their own choices. Campaigners agree in principle but want the {{9}} to be clearer. Until then, shoppers can protect themselves with one simple {{10}}: turn the packet over and read the small print before you decide.

选 J. precise。no precise legal meaning 意为没有明确的法律含义，修饰 legal meaning 最贴切；generous 意为慷慨的，与此处语义无关。
选 K. refer。refer to 意为指的是，此处说明包装上的数字对应的是哪一份的量；decline 意为下降，不能与 to 构成此义。
选 M. similar。similar values 意为相近的数值，同类产品的营养成分更容易比较；frequently 是副词，不能修饰名词 values。
选 B. avoid。avoid products 意为避开这类产品，与前文「成分表越短加工越少」的观点一致；maintain products 搭配不当。
选 N. warn。warn that 意为提醒、警告，营养学家提醒消费者糖会以多种名称出现；decline 后接 that 从句表示拒绝，语义不符。
选 H. harmless。look harmless 意为看起来无害，与前面暗中含多种甜味剂形成对比；generous 不能描述食品是否无害。

选 A. advantage。a consistent advantage 意为持续的优势，冒号后正是这项优势的具体内容；warning 意为警告，与语境不符。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A change in attitudes Ten years ago, buying second-hand clothes was something many young people did quietly, if at all. Today the same shoppers post pictures of their finds online and discuss them openly. The stigma that once surrounded used goods has largely disappeared, and a generation that grew up with recycling at school seems to see resale as a sensible habit rather than a sign of poverty.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Cheaper than buying new The most obvious attraction is price. A coat that costs eighty pounds in a shop may sell for fifteen on a resale platform, and popular brands keep a surprisingly high share of their value. For students and young families in particular, this makes a wider range of clothing affordable, and many users say they now buy more thoughtfully because they know an item can be sold on later.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Better for the planet Every garment that is worn for a second time means one fewer new item produced, and clothing production is a significant source of carbon emissions and water use. Environmental groups have been quick to point this out, and several platforms now calculate the estimated savings for each sale. Critics note, however, that the overall volume of clothing bought continues to rise, which may cancel out some of the benefit.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A social experience For many users, the appeal goes beyond money and the environment. Buyers and sellers exchange messages, negotiate prices and often meet in person to hand over the goods. These small conversations turn a transaction into something closer to a community activity, and friendships have been known to start over a pair of boots.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Problems for traditional shops The shift has not been welcomed everywhere. Several high-street chains have reported declining sales among younger customers, and some have responded by launching their own resale schemes. Shop owners argue that the platforms enjoy an unfair advantage because they carry no stock, though others insist that the two ways of shopping can coexist.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: What the future may bring Analysts expect the second-hand market to keep expanding, possibly overtaking fast fashion within a decade. Growth brings its own questions: how to keep counterfeits off the platforms, how to protect sellers' personal data, and whether resale income should be taxed. Most observers agree that some form of regulation is now likely, and the platforms themselves say clearer rules would help.

Young consumers no longer regard used goods as something to be ashamed of.
By extending the life of clothing, the trend helps to cut carbon emissions.

Experts expect the market to keep growing, although regulation may be needed.
